decision: Not adopted: a name-based signal in reconcile_memory_index.py --check-misplaced that flags a fact naming another level's project by name, beside the existing absolute-path signal.
reopen_if: A name signal is found that, over a real store, flags no more than a few facts beyond the confirmed misfiles.
why: Disproven by measurement: a prototype over a real store of about 500 facts flagged roughly a third of them, against a true misfile rate near one, because a fact names a tool or project as its subject far more often than as its location. A path is a location claim, a bare name is a topic mention, and a stopword list would have to drop exactly the names that matter.

anchors: Before queueing against `skill:<name>` (cases 1 and 2), read that skill's declined list
decision: Before queueing a fix against skill:<name>, read that skill's rejected and removed decisions with skill_decisions.py show; a lesson that re-proposes a listed entry is queued only with a --why that answers its reopen_if and names its id, otherwise it is not queued and the report says so.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: plan approval for the per-skill decision ledger, including its readers in self-improve

reopen_if: Captures keep queueing proposals the ledger already declines although they ran show, or the ledger stops shipping with the skill.
why: A closed queue entry does not stop a reworded lesson being queued again, so a declined proposal came back in later sessions; the skill's ledger is the record a capture can read before queueing.

anchors: also record it as a `rejected` entry in that skill's ledger in the source repo
decision: When a skill-targeted queue entry is dropped as disproven or declined for a reason that will still hold, it is also recorded as a rejected entry in that skill's ledger in the source repo through skill_decisions.py add --from-file; a close because it shipped or duplicates another entry records nothing.

reopen_if: Ledger rejected entries written at drop time turn out to be mostly stale or wrong when later read, or the queue gains a reader that blocks reworded re-proposals itself.
why: The queue tombstone is not read when a reworded proposal is queued; only a ledger entry reaches the next session that reads the skill's declined list.
